experiment.name: phase1_hamming_weight
description: Does the operand-movement leakage scale with operand Hamming weight, and
how steeply?
Phase 1 so far establishes that leakage lives in operand movement rather
than in the vector ALU, and that the per-byte cost rises ~68x from an
L1-resident working set to a DRAM-resident one. Both were measured at a
single contrast, HW 0 against HW 32. This sweeps the operand value while
holding everything else fixed, which is the measurement the leakage model
P = a + b*HW needs.
Victim is ws_l3_x8, chosen over ws_dram_x8 deliberately: the depth sweep
gives it the largest absolute effect (+1.85 W, replicated) and a detector
that reaches 1.000, whereas ws_dram_x8 has the higher per-byte cost but
worse detectability. Largest pJ/byte is not the same as best conditioned.
Condition 0 is HW 0 in every run and condition 1 is the test pattern, so
each run reads as 'power at HW k relative to an all-zero working set'.
The polarity control established that the condition index itself carries
no bias (B = +0.7 +/- 3.1 mW over eight A/A runs), so no reverse arm is
needed here; one A/A is carried anyway as the per-session gate.
Bit placement is decorrelated from Hamming weight: HW 4, 8, 16 and 24 each
run two independent random patterns of that weight (seeded, listed below),
so a difference between patterns at equal HW measures sensitivity to which
bits are set, and averaging over patterns leaves HW itself. Structured
values such as 0x55555555 are avoided on purpose -- a periodic pattern
could interact with bus or DRAM encoding and would not be a clean HW probe.
What this does NOT measure: Hamming distance. ws_fill replicates one 32-bit
value across the whole buffer, so consecutive transferred words are
identical and the HD between them is zero by construction. That is the
point -- it isolates the static HW effect. Separating HW from HD needs a
victim that alternates two operands at fixed HW, which is the next
experiment.
warmup_blocks is 4 throughout: ws_l3_x8 populates 2 x 4 MB per thread, far
less than the ws_dram_x8 case that motivated the flag, but the cost is
half a second per run and it removes the question.

runs.label: hw32
runs.comment: HW 32, 0xFFFFFFFF. Directly comparable to l3_forward in phase1_polarity.
